title: A Choir for the Garden
premise: Mara Winterbourne has spent her life tending the Hollow Gate, the ward that keeps the valley of Vell safe from the starless country beyond — a land erased from every map and memory when its people bargained their existence away to survive a plague of forgetting. When the wards collapse, Mara discovers the gate was never a barrier but a choir: ten voices, each a keeper across generations, whose song holds Vell inside the world. Pulled into the vanished country with a disgraced cartographer named Ilex and a child who remembers too much, Mara must gather the scattered verses of the song before the last star goes out and both countries are unmade. In the end she learns her own mother's voice was the first verse sold away, and rather than restore the old order, Mara teaches the forgotten country to sing for itself — dissolving the gate entirely so that memory, like weather, can cross freely in both directions.
about_author: Casper Brightwater is the pen name of a former church organist who grew up in a river valley where the fog arrives on schedule and never explains itself. They write fantasy about doors, debts, and the people paid to keep them shut.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Quiet
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A portrait of routine: oiling the Gate's hinges, reciting the valley's names aloud each dusk so they stay remembered. The emotional beat is contentment laced with loneliness — Mara has never questioned why magic cannot follow her past the treeline, or why no one else ever volunteers for the work.

chapters.title: Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The stars vanish at moonrise; the Gate's hum falters into silence; the border wards fall like cut strings. Ilex, a cartographer exiled for mapping what shouldn't exist, stumbles out of the dark carrying a compass that points at memories instead of north. Beat: dread and reluctant alliance as the valley's edge simply stops being there.

chapters.title: The Country That Isn't
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. Crossing into the erased land: fields mid-harvest, tables set for meals, all frozen and fading. They find Wren, an eight-year-old who remembers everything the country forgot, including Mara's mother. Beat: uncanny grief — survival here means being slowly deleted, and Wren is the only one still fighting it.

chapters.title: What the Bargain Bought
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Through the child's memories we learn the truth: generations ago the country traded its name, history, and songs to a thing called the Hush in exchange for surviving the plague of forgetting. Beat: horror reframed as pity — the villains were desperate people, and the debt compounds with interest.

chapters.title: Ten Voices, One Song
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. The compass leads them to the ruins of the Choirhouse, where they learn the Gate is sung, not built — ten keepers' voices braided into one verse per generation. Mara's mother was the tenth voice, and she didn't die; she was taken as collateral. Beat: betrayal and resolve hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Hush Offers Terms
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The Hush manifests as a courteous absence and offers Mara a deal: her mother returned, the valley spared, if she delivers Wren — the last complete memory of the country — as final payment. Beat: temptation sharpened by love; Mara says yes before she can stop herself, and hates it.

chapters.title: Verses in the Bone
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Racing the dimming sky, the trio recovers three lost verses hidden in a drowned bell tower, a soldier's skeleton still standing sentry, and Ilex's own suppressed childhood. Beat: bittersweet wonder — recovering memory hurts, but each verse makes them more real than the country around them.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Confession
chapters.summary: Ilex's POV. Ilex admits he was hired by Vell's council years ago to find the Choirhouse and end the singing forever, freeing the valley from paying keepers — his exile was staged to hide his success. Beat: shattering trust; Mara must decide whether the man who broke the song can help finish it.

chapters.title: The Last Star
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At the Choirhouse altar, with one star left, Mara sings the recovered verses while Ilex holds the Hush at bay and Wren anchors them with total recall. Her mother's voice rises through her — then Mara breaks the bargain, refusing to hand over Wren, and offers the Hush something unprecedented: a new verse written by the forgotten themselves. Beat: climax — sacrifice transmuted into invitation.

chapters.title: A Choir for the Garden
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The Hush, which was only ever hunger for being remembered, accepts the new verse and becomes the eleventh voice. The Gate dissolves; the two countries braid back together; fog now carries songs both ways. Mara plants a garden over the old threshold where anyone may come sing. Beat: quiet, earned hope — power given away instead of kept.
